description: We are a small team of three philologists with a strong interest in storytelling, communication, design, ethics, and making complex scientific ideas understandable to a wider audience.
summary:
Our project looks at two basic needs of any future lunar base — food and shelter. For plants, we chose three very different places on Earth. The Deccan Traps help us study basaltic material, Socompa shows how life copes with extreme environmental stress, and Sambhar gives us a way to explore salinity, alkalinity, and biological adaptation.
For shelter, we looked at Korea’s Third Tunnel as an operational analog for turning an underground rock space into a protected, pressurized habitat while reducing the amount of material brought from Earth.
None of these places is “the Moon on Earth,” and that is exactly the point. Each one lets us explore a specific problem while keeping its limitations clear. Together, they show what Earth can teach us before we go to the Moon.
details:
The first looks for Earth soils and mineral substrates that share some key properties with lunar regolith. These materials could be used to test how plants grow under difficult conditions.

The second asks whether an existing underground space could become part of a future lunar habitat and reduce the amount of structural material that must be brought from Earth.
